title: Rules and diagnostics
body: Rules are grouped like in Biome: syntax, schema, graph, text, markdown, style, trace, build, meta and custom. A rule is written by its name, like in ESLint and Biome (style/hedging), in the rules of docc.json and in docIgnore; its code such as DOC301 is a public contract that never changes and still works there, with a DOC902 warning that names the rule. Retired codes are not reused. A diagnostic, docc rules and docc explain show the name first, then the code. Three rules were renamed to say what they check: style/timeless-words is style/time-bound-words, schema/unregistered is schema/unregistered-tag and trace/unknown-id is trace/bad-code-tag; the old names work like the codes. Messages are in English and every message has a hint. docc reports problems and changes nothing in the sources: there are no automatic fixes. ^dkac

The preset recommended gives every rule a default level, and every rule is on by default. The rules style/hedging (DOC352) and style/time-bound-words (DOC353) warn about vague and time-bound words. Word rules, the repeated-word rule and custom rules match text in Unicode NFC and skip text in backticks, so an identifier such as `new` is written in backticks. ^x9db

Core rules are always errors and cannot be suppressed, switched off or given another level: broken JSON, duplicate keys, a missing title, invalid ids, the built-in schema, a missing kind schema (DOC109), duplicate ids, broken references, orphans, parent cycles, missing roots, links to hidden documents, bad includes, stale link hashes (DOC209), duplicate block codes (DOC212), blocks without a code (DOC216), broken image paths (DOC213), bad code tags (DOC401), changed code (DOC402) and stale output (DOC501). ^j3y5
Rule levels are set in [[config@jsqc]]; the commands that run the rules are in [[commands@nmzt]]; version hashes are described in [[document-model#change_tracking@m95u]]. ^yr83
notable_rules: DOC209 graph/suspect-link reports a link whose version hash is missing or no longer matches its target, with the change and the hash the target has now. DOC110 syntax/reserved-field-typo warns about a free field spelled almost like a reserved key (`parnet`, `hiden`). DOC202 names the nearest existing ids. DOC310 markdown/raw-html also reports links with a `javascript:`, `vbscript:` or `data:` address; docc does not rewrite them. DOC402 trace/code-changed reports a code file or region whose fingerprint is missing or no longer matches: the documents it points to may no longer agree with the code. DOC112 syntax/invalid-comment reports a malformed item of `$comments` or an id used by another comment; DOC215 graph/comment-lost warns that a comment lost its place and asks to move its pointer or delete it. ^9gb4

DOC212 graph/duplicate-anchor reports a block code on two blocks of the project or equal to a heading anchor of its page; DOC216 graph/missing-code a block without a code. DOC213 graph/broken-file reports an image path that names no file in the sources, lies outside them or is not a png, jpg, jpeg, gif, svg or webp file. DOC214 graph/wrong-target-kind reports a reference whose target kind is not allowed by `x-docc-target`. ^x7kj

DOC314 style/manual-number warns when `numbering` is on and a title or a section key starts with its own number. DOC403 trace/uncovered warns when a document of a kind with `x-docc-covered` has no code tag. DOC303 also catches `N/A`, a lone dash, `see above` and `works correctly`, and their Russian forms. ^ktfm
diagnostic_format: Text form: file:line:column: level CODE (group/name) message, followed by a line with the hint, then a summary line such as checked 3 files: 1 error, 0 warnings. JSON form: an envelope with a summary (checked, errors, warnings, shown, truncated) and a diagnostics array of objects with code, rule, level, file, line, column, endLine, endColumn, message and hint. When the output is cut by max-diagnostics, truncated is true. ^fqs9
The order is deterministic: level, file path, line, column, code, rule name. Columns count Unicode characters of the source text, also inside strings with escape sequences. ^vw9t
see_also: Run `docc rules` for the list with current levels and `docc explain` with a code for a description and an example. ^kupg
